Hi Alyssa — quick answers ahead of the call and a request for the test plan details so we can prepare runbooks: 

Hyperscaler comparison (high level):
- Latency: On comparable GPUs, Redwood's serving runtime shows lower tail latency for chat workloads because of continuous batching + KV cache optimizations we built for long-context sessions. Expect 10-30% lower p95 in our internal benchmarks on conversational loads.
- Throughput: We do automatic batching and can sustain higher aggregated throughput for many small concurrent requests; hyperscalers can scale horizontally but often at higher per-token cost due to multi-tenant pricing.
- Pricing model: Hyperscalers often bundle infra + model licensing; Redwood separates model variant pricing + serving unit economics so customers can choose quantized model variants for cost control.

OpenAI-compat notes:
- API surface: We support OpenAI-compatible shapes (chat/completions/embeddings) and provide an SDK shim so switching is typically a few lines of code. The biggest diffs are in streaming semantics (we offer chunked deltas similar to OpenAI but also support structured tool-calling hooks) and rate-limit headers.
- Prompt/response parity: For base models aligned to the same weights, parity is high. Differences arise when providers apply different sampling defaults or safety filters. We recommend freezing model config (temp/top_p/stop) to minimize diffs and adding a short calibration set in the test plan to flag regressions.

What we need from FinCo to prep:
- A sample of 20-30 representative prompts (high-risk flows flagged) and expected outputs or acceptance criteria.
- Baseline throughput expectations (RPS) for each test scenario.

I attached the short hyperscaler comparison PDF and the API compatibility guide. We'll use those as reference in the session.

Camila
